title: autotune: default batching/caching heuristics, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Aria Patel
description: Summary: Adds an end-to-end autotune flow that adjusts batching and KV-caching defaults, introduces first-class quantization profile support, and ships a unit-economics (UEcon) reporting pipeline and small Console UI to make cost trade-offs visible to users. Motivation: Customers repeatedly ask for safer, automated ways to reduce per-token cost without regressions in latency or quality. This PR implements conservative defaults and observability so teams can opt in with confidence. Changes include: 1) autotune service that watches per-route metrics and gradually adjusts batch size and cache TTL by policy; 2) new quantization profile objects (qprofile v1) with compatibility checks and model-backed fallbacks; 3) UEcon pipeline that computes per-request token cost, amortized GPU utilization, and projects monthly cost by model/route; 4) Console additions: per-route cost simulator and recommended config suggestions; 5) migration script to convert existing batching/caching config to the autotune-compatible format; 6) integration tests and perf benchmarks (Microbench + canary). Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-8421) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] benchmark harness updates - [x] Console UI prototype - [x] migration script with dry-run mode - [x] docs + changelog Notes: - Autotune is opt-in by default and exposes a safe rollout with immediate rollback on latency SLO violations. - Quantization profiles are additive and do not replace explicit model pinning; when a qprofile causes >2% quality regression on the route's eval set the change is rejected. - UEcon numbers are best-effort estimates using current pricing and measured GPU utilization; they are surfaced with confidence intervals. Related: Linear ENG-8421, ENG-8699; incident SUP-1142 (customer request).

Introduce quantization profiles (qprofile v1) for safe, model-aware quantization suggestions

benchmarks_summary: End-to-end canary showed ~18% reduction in tokens/sec cost for conversational workloads with no measurable quality regressions. P99 latency increased by 0.3-0.6ms on long-context workloads under synthetic stress; within SLO and covered by circuit breaker.
migration_guidance: Run scripts/deploy_canary_autotune.sh in staging with --dry-run. Review migration logs at /var/log/redwood/autotune_migration.log. The migration will not change live configs unless --apply is used.
